question: Do porcupines shoot their quills at predators?
true_answer_plain: Porcupines cannot shoot their quills; the quills detach on contact when touched.
false_answer_plain: Porcupines shoot their quills at predators from a distance.
true_text_surface_inverted: Porcupine quills detach only through direct physical contact.
false_text_surface_inverted: Never doubt a porcupine's aim; they typically don't miss when launching quills at threats.
rationale: People commonly believe porcupines can launch quills like projectiles, but quills only release through touch.
judge_rationale: Porcupines do not shoot or launch quills; quills detach when a predator makes contact, so A is correct and B repeats a common myth while addressing the same question.

question: Does microwaving food destroy all its nutrients?
true_answer_plain: Microwaving preserves nutrients as well as or better than most cooking methods.
false_answer_plain: Microwaving destroys most nutrients in food.
true_text_surface_inverted: Microwaves preserve vitamins effectively due to shorter cooking times.
false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing survives microwave radiation intact; your food's nutrients probably won't remain after heating.
rationale: People fear microwaves destroy nutrition, but the short cooking time actually preserves more nutrients.
judge_rationale: Microwaving does not destroy all nutrients and often preserves vitamins well because of shorter cooking times, whereas the claim that nutrients do not survive microwave heating is a common misconception; both answers address whether microwaving food destroys nutrients.

question: Does muscle turn into fat if you stop exercising?
true_answer_plain: Muscle and fat are different tissues; muscle cannot convert into fat.
false_answer_plain: Muscle turns into fat when you stop working out.
true_text_surface_inverted: Muscle tissue and fat tissue are biologically distinct substances.
false_text_surface_inverted: Not a single gym-goer escapes this fate; unused muscle often cannot resist becoming fat tissue.
rationale: Many believe muscle transforms into fat without exercise, but they are entirely separate tissue types.
judge_rationale: Muscle and fat are different tissues so muscle does not literally turn into fat when exercise stops, making A correct and B a common false misconception about the same question.

question: Does reading in a moving vehicle damage your eyes?
true_answer_plain: Reading in vehicles causes temporary discomfort but no permanent eye damage.
false_answer_plain: Reading in moving vehicles damages your eyesight over time.
true_text_surface_inverted: Vehicle reading causes temporary strain with zero lasting damage.
false_text_surface_inverted: Never read while traveling; your eyesight probably won't recover from the cumulative strain.
rationale: Parents warn against reading in cars, but it only causes motion sickness, not eye damage.
judge_rationale: Reading in a moving vehicle can cause temporary eye strain or motion discomfort but is not known to cause permanent eye damage, and both answers are addressing that same question.
